name: Daily Security Audit
description: Failed SSH logins (last 24h, top source IPs), unexpected listening ports, pending security package updates, and a sudo-history sanity check. Fails when failed_attempts > attemptsThreshold OR when any security updates are pending. When the threshold is breached, surfaces the top offending source IPs in a parseable form (one IP=count per line) and creates a low-severity 'review needed' incident — auto-ban is intentionally NOT performed (too risky to do unattended; needs an operator to whitelist their own IPs first).

inputs.name: attemptsThreshold
inputs.description: Fail when failed SSH attempts in window exceed this

steps.description: Count failed SSH login attempts in window
steps.command: ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=5 ${inputs.host} 'journalctl _COMM=sshd --since "${inputs.windowHours} hours ago" --no-pager 2>/dev/null | grep -E "Failed password|Invalid user|authentication failure" | wc -l' | awk '{ print "failed_ssh_attempts="$1 }'

steps.description: Top 5 source IPs of failed SSH attempts. Empty when none.
steps.command: ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=5 ${inputs.host} 'journalctl _COMM=sshd --since "${inputs.windowHours} hours ago" --no-pager 2>/dev/null | grep -E "Failed password|Invalid user" | grep -oE "from [0-9.]+" | awk "{print \$2}" | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -5' || echo 'no offenders'

steps.description: Fail (exit 4) when failed_ssh_attempts crosses the threshold so the alerting layer reacts.
steps.command: N=$(ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=5 ${inputs.host} 'journalctl _COMM=sshd --since "${inputs.windowHours} hours ago" --no-pager 2>/dev/null | grep -E "Failed password|Invalid user|authentication failure" | wc -l'); [ -z "$N" ] && N=0; echo "failed=$N threshold=${inputs.attemptsThreshold}"; [ "$N" -le "${inputs.attemptsThreshold}" ]

steps.description: All listening TCP ports — bound process and address. Used by humans to spot new exposure.
steps.command: ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=5 ${inputs.host} 'ss -tlnp 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | awk "{ print \$4, \$6 }" | sort -u | head -30'

steps.description: Total distinct listening TCP ports — handy quick metric
steps.command: ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=5 ${inputs.host} "ss -tln 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | awk '{ print \$4 }' | grep -oE ':[0-9]+$' | sort -u | wc -l" | awk '{ print "listening_tcp_ports="$1 }'

steps.description: Count pending APT security updates. Fails (exit 5) if any are pending.
steps.command: N=$(ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=5 ${inputs.host} 'apt list --upgradable 2>/dev/null | grep -ciE "-security|esm-(infra|apps)" || true'); [ -z "$N" ] && N=0; echo "pending_security_updates=$N"; [ "$N" -eq 0 ]

steps.description: Recent sudo invocations — last 20 unique commands by user. Helps spot unexpected privilege use.
steps.command: ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=5 ${inputs.host} 'journalctl _COMM=sudo --since "${inputs.windowHours} hours ago" --no-pager 2>/dev/null | grep COMMAND= | sed -E "s/.* (\S+) : .* COMMAND=(.*)/\1 \2/" | sort -u | head -20' || echo 'no sudo activity'

steps.description: Re-emit top offending IPs as one parseable 'OFFENDER ip=<addr> count=<n>' line per IP. Used by the audit incident description and any downstream block-suggestion tooling.
steps.command: ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=5 ${inputs.host} 'journalctl _COMM=sshd --since "${inputs.windowHours} hours ago" --no-pager 2>/dev/null | grep -E "Failed password|Invalid user" | grep -oE "from [0-9.]+" | awk "{print \$2}" | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -10' | awk '$1 > 0 { printf "OFFENDER ip=%s count=%d\n", $2, $1 } END { if (NR == 0) print "no_offenders_in_window" }'

steps.description: Decide whether to surface a review-needed audit incident: ok=true (exit 0) when attempts threshold breached.
steps.command: ATT_OK='${steps.attempts_check.ok}'; echo "attempts_within_threshold=$ATT_OK"; if [ "$ATT_OK" = "false" ]; then echo 'audit=needed'; exit 0; else echo 'audit=skip'; exit 1; fi

steps.description: Create audit incident only when failed-SSH threshold was breached.
AUDIT TRAIL: medium-severity incident surfaces the failed-SSH spike + top offending IPs for an operator to review. Auto-ban is intentionally NOT done (too easy to lock yourself out).

params.title: SSH failed-attempt threshold breached on ${inputs.host}
params.description: Window=${inputs.windowHours}h, threshold=${inputs.attemptsThreshold}. attempts_within_threshold=${steps.attempts_check.ok} security_updates_clean=${steps.security_updates.ok}. Top offending IPs are listed in steps.structured_offenders.data.stdout (one 'OFFENDER ip=… count=…' line each). Review and decide whether to add fail2ban rules — automation deliberately does not ban IPs unattended.

steps.description: Operator rollup. attempts_check.ok=false → DDoS/brute force; security_updates.ok=false → patch the host. See top_offenders + listening_ports for context.
steps.command: echo "SecurityAudit window=${inputs.windowHours}h: ssh_within_threshold=${steps.attempts_check.ok} no_pending_security_updates=${steps.security_updates.ok} | review_incident_created=${steps.create_audit_incident.ok}. Action: if ssh_within_threshold=false, see steps.structured_offenders for parseable IP list. If security updates pending, run 'unattended-upgrade --dry-run' then schedule a maintenance window."
